puzzles.description: Arrange the 9 tiles to reveal your desk assignment
hints: Tap two tiles to swap them. The poster spells WELCOME, then your desk number.
Top row spells 'WEL'. Middle row spells 'COM'. Last row finishes the word and the number.
Row 1: W E L / Row 2: C O M / Row 3: E 7 B

puzzles.description: Match each cable to the correct port on your EC2 workstation

falseOutputs: A faint smell of plastic. Try again.

hints: Match each color/label to its obvious port. Power → PWR.
Power → PWR, Data → I/O, Ground → GND. One left.
Power → PWR, Data → I/O, Ground → GND, Network → NET.

puzzles.description: Enter your 4-digit IAM PIN — the year AWS launched
hints: Your Desk Assignment Slip has the PIN. It's the year AWS launched as a service.
AWS S3 launched in March 2006 — the same year AWS itself officially started selling cloud services.

puzzles.description: Talk to Alex, your orientation buddy

config.name: Alex
config.greeting: FINALLY. I thought Frank ate you. Sit. I made you a sticky note. I make these for everyone — it's my thing now.

lines.label: What's the boot sequence?
lines.response: IAM first, ALWAYS — no auth, no party. Then VPC, gotta have a network or your packets just sit there crying. Then EC2 — your workstation comes online. Then S3 — locker mounts. Then Lambda — let the functions cook. Memorize it. Trust me. Don't reorder. Karen reordered. Karen got reset.

lines.label: Wait — what happens if you reorder?
lines.response: Skip IAM and the locker just… ignores you forever. Boot EC2 before VPC and your workstation has no network — just yells into the void. Lambda before S3 and your functions have nowhere to write, they spiral, it's tragic. Pick your disaster. Don't reorder.

lines.label: Who's Karen?
lines.response: Karen was the orientation buddy before me. Reordered the boot sequence on day one. Now she works in… 'Compliance.' We don't talk about it.

lines.label: Any tips for Frank?
lines.response: Frank looks scary. Frank is scary. But he made the LAMBDAS poster himself in PowerPoint and he is incredibly proud. Compliment the poster. He'll cry. Lovely man.

lines.label: Got it. Heading to the Server Room.
lines.response: Go go go. Tap badge, drag tiles, hit confirm. Once you boot it, swag's yours. T-shirt, stickers, the cold brew on tap. We'll celebrate at the Lambda Café. GO.

hints: Click each dialog option to learn the boot order before heading to the Server Room.
Alex tells you the order on the very first option: IAM, VPC, EC2, S3, Lambda.
Read the sticky note Alex hands you (card 402) — it lists the boot order verbatim.

puzzles.description: Drag the five service tiles into the correct boot order
hints: Auth first, then network, then compute, then storage, then functions.
IAM must come before everything (no auth, no access). Lambda comes last (it depends on everything).
Order: IAM → VPC → EC2 → S3 → Lambda.
